findings.title: Closing a timed-until interval can change probability at time zero
findings.counterexample: A singleton absorbing p-state gives probability 0 for (not top) U^(0,1] p and probability 1 after replacing the interval by [0,1].
findings.remaining_book_work: Correct the unrestricted interval-closure assertion and preserve endpoint flags wherever they affect timed-until semantics; state and support exact hypotheses for any restricted equivalence used by an algorithm.
findings.status: Confirmed from the current definitions by two readers; not repaired during inventory.

findings.title: Printed nominal saturation misses a forced subsumption and its quotient labels disagree
findings.counterexample: A <= exists r.C, A <= exists s.D, C <= {a}, D <= {a}, C <= P, D <= Q, P and Q <= bottom entails A empty and A <= P; the printed saturation stops without P or bottom in S(A) and without bottom at a nominal.
findings.remaining_book_work: Repair the nominal/nonemptiness handling and decision/canonical-model proof, or accurately restrict the claimed algorithm. A fresh-nominal preprocessing direction is not an implemented or verified correction.
findings.status: Confirmed against all printed rules and the current decision claim by two readers; source correspondence does not establish correctness; not repaired during inventory.

findings.title: CTL illustration omits the root valuation needed by its AF claim
findings.counterexample: If p holds at the unlabeled root, inclusive AF p is true immediately, contrary to the annotation; the intended false value requires p false at that root.
findings.remaining_book_work: Make the intended root atomic valuation explicit in the figure or an accompanying valuation definition.
findings.status: Already included in original apparatus row A-146; not an extra original requirement and not a counterexample to CTL semantics.
